title: Context API & Redux Toolkit: Global State Architecture in TypeScript
description: Master React Context for scoped global state and Redux Toolkit (RTK) for complex predictable state with TypeScript: createSlice, createAsyncThunk, RTK Query, and performance optimization with selector memoization.

data.text: Choosing Between Context and Redux Toolkit

React Context and Redux Toolkit (RTK) are not competitors—they serve different purposes. Context is appropriate for slowly-changing global state consumed by many components: authentication, theme, locale, and feature flags. RTK is appropriate for high-frequency state changes, complex async workflows, cross-slice derived state, and scenarios requiring DevTools time-travel debugging. In an enterprise AI assistant, the user's auth state and theme live in Context; the conversation list, streaming state machine, and agent tool results live in RTK.

data.text: RTK's `createSlice` generates action creators and reducers from a single declaration, eliminating the boilerplate of classic Redux. `createAsyncThunk` manages the `pending/fulfilled/rejected` lifecycle of async operations automatically.

data.content: A fully typed RTK slice managing conversation loading state, active session, and optimistic message appending.

data.text: RTK re-exports `createSelector` from Reselect. Memoized selectors prevent expensive derivations (like filtering 500 messages) from running on every Redux state change.

data.title: Memoized Selector for Active Conversation Messages
data.content: The filtered messages list only recomputes when conversations or activeId actually change.

data.title: Context & Redux Toolkit Architecture Checklist
items: Context used only for slowly-changing global state (auth, theme, locale, feature flags)
RTK slices own domain state with typed actions, reducers, and async thunks
createSelector used for all derived state to prevent expensive redundant recalculations
RTK Query considered for server state instead of createAsyncThunk to avoid manual caching
Context providers do not contain heavy computation that re-renders all consumers on every state change
Redux DevTools extension enabled in development for time-travel debugging

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: Context is ideal for slowly-changing cross-cutting concerns; RTK for complex domain state.
createSlice dramatically reduces Redux boilerplate with full TypeScript inference.
Memoized selectors with createSelector prevent expensive derivations on every state update.
Next, we master TanStack Query for treating server-fetched data as a first-class reactive cache.
data.takeaway: Use the right tool for the state category: Context for auth/theme, RTK for complex domain state machines, and TanStack Query for server state.
